title: Free water refill taps across the city
summary: Scottish Water's Top Up Tap map shows free public water refill points across Scotland, including Edinburgh, so you can top up a bottle on a hot day instead of buying one.
details: Find your nearest tap using the online Top Up Tap map
Over 70 taps across Scotland including cities, parks and beaches
Bring your own refillable bottle - no charge
Part of Scottish Water's Your Water Your Life campaign

sources.title: Scottish Water: Top Up Tap Map

title: Council advice on staying cool and safe in hot weather
summary: Edinburgh Council's hot weather page gives practical steps for staying cool and checking on vulnerable neighbours during heat, and links to Met Office and NHS guidance.
details: Avoid the hottest part of the day, 11am to 3pm
Close curtains and windows during the day, open them at night to cool the home
Carry water and wear a hat and sunscreen outdoors
Check on older or vulnerable neighbours and relatives
Links through to Met Office forecasts and NHS hot weather advice

sources.title: City of Edinburgh Council: Keeping cool in hot weather

title: Suggest a spot for a new street tree
summary: Edinburgh's One Million Tree City programme aims to plant around 250,000 trees by 2030 for shade and cooling. Residents can suggest planting locations or record trees they've already planted, though the scheme doesn't hand out free trees to individuals.
details: Aims for roughly 250,000 new trees by 2030 as part of the city's net zero target
Submit a tree-planting suggestion through the council's online form
Report a tree you've already planted so it counts towards the total
Contact edinburghmilliontrees@edinburgh.gov.uk with questions

sources.title: City of Edinburgh Council: One million tree city

title: Check today's air quality before you go out
summary: The Scottish Air Quality database gives near real-time pollution readings from monitoring stations across Scotland, including Edinburgh, via an interactive map.
details: Interactive map shows readings from monitoring sites across Scotland
Filter by pollutant, e.g. nitrogen dioxide, PM2.5, PM10
Data updates near real-time, with a last-updated time shown on the site
Free to use, no login needed

sources.title: Scottish Air Quality: monitoring network

title: Sign up for air pollution email alerts
summary: Free email bulletins from the Scottish Air Quality Database can flag Edinburgh readings, forecasts, or alerts when pollution is high, so you can plan around bad air days.
details: Choose the 'City of Edinburgh' region when registering
Pick measurements, forecasts, alerts, or a combination
Set the frequency: daily, hourly, or only when pollution is high
Free, and you can unsubscribe any time by email

sources.title: Scottish Air Quality: Email bulletin registration

title: Low Emission Zone in the city centre
summary: Edinburgh's Low Emission Zone covers the city centre and restricts the most polluting vehicles to help cut traffic pollution; fines apply to non-compliant vehicles.
details: Covers roughly 1.2 square miles of the city centre, enforced 24/7 by cameras
Petrol vehicles need Euro 4 or above; diesel needs Euro 6 or above
Zero-emission and electric vehicles always comply
Penalty charge notices have been issued since 1 June 2024
Check your vehicle using the free LEZ Scotland registration checker

sources.title: City of Edinburgh Council: Low Emission Zone
mygov.scot: Low Emission Zones

title: Home Energy Scotland grant and loan for insulation and heating
summary: Scottish Government grants, plus an optional interest-free loan, help homeowners pay for insulation, heat pumps and other clean heating upgrades.
details: Heat pumps and heat networks: up to £7,500 grant plus up to £7,500 loan
Solid wall insulation: up to £7,500 grant plus up to £2,500 loan
Loft, cavity or underfloor insulation: up to £1,500 grant plus up to £500 loan
Extra £1,500 available in remote, rural or off-gas areas
First-come, first-served - funding is not unlimited

sources.title: Home Energy Scotland: Grant and Loan

title: Free insulation and heating through Warmer Homes Scotland
summary: Warmer Homes Scotland can fully fund insulation, draught-proofing and heating upgrades worth £10,000 or more for eligible homeowners and private tenants on low incomes or with health needs.
details: For homeowners or private tenants living in the home as their main residence for 6+ months
Household must include someone 75+, someone with a qualifying medical condition, or someone on a passport benefit such as Universal Credit
Covers wall and loft insulation, draught-proofing, central heating and renewables
The Scottish Government meets most or all of the cost
Call 0808 808 2282 or use the online eligibility checker

sources.title: Home Energy Scotland: Warmer Homes Scotland

title: Free, impartial energy advice and a funding finder
summary: Home Energy Scotland's advisors give free, impartial phone advice on cutting energy bills and can point you to whichever grant, loan or scheme actually fits your home.
details: Freephone advice line: 0808 808 2282
Online funding finder tool checks which schemes you might qualify for
Covers the Home Energy Scotland Grant and Loan, Warmer Homes Scotland, landlord loans and the Warm Home Discount
Free for homeowners, landlords and tenants

sources.title: Home Energy Scotland: Find funding

title: Sign up for free flood warnings from Floodline
summary: SEPA's Floodline service sends free flood warnings and alerts by email for your postcode, covering Edinburgh's rivers including the Water of Leith.
details: Register online with your email and postcode at myfloodline.sepa.org.uk
Get targeted 'Flood Warning' messages for your immediate area or wider 'Flood Alert' messages for the region
Free service - no account needed just to check current warnings
No email? Call Floodline on 0345 988 1188, option 2 for Scotland then option 3 for an advisor

sources.title: SEPA: Sign up to Floodline

title: What to do and who to call during a flood
summary: Edinburgh Council's flood page tells residents to shut off power and water at the mains, avoid contact with floodwater, and gives a number to call to report flooding.
details: Report flooding to the council on 0131 200 2000
Switch off electricity at the fuse box and water at the mains if flooding starts
Floodwater can be contaminated - keep children and pets away from it
Check on elderly or vulnerable neighbours
Sign up to SEPA's flood warnings and monitor local radio and council social media during alerts

sources.title: City of Edinburgh Council: What to do in a flood

title: Report a blocked or overflowing sewer
summary: Scottish Water runs a free 24/7 line for reporting flooding from blocked or overflowing sewers and drains.
details: Freephone 24/7 reporting line: 0800 0778778
Use this for flooding caused by sewers or drains rather than surface water or rivers
Confirmed directly on Scottish Water's own sewer flooding page

sources.title: Scottish Water: Sewer flooding

title: Hire an e-bike with Voi
summary: Voi runs Edinburgh's e-bike hire scheme - dockless bikes you unlock and pay for through the Voi app, good for short trips instead of driving. This replaced the old docked Just Eat Cycles scheme, which shut down in 2020.
details: Pay-as-you-go: £0.49 to unlock, then £0.11 a minute
Day and monthly passes work out cheaper per ride for frequent riders - check the app for current prices
Dockless - park at any safe street location rather than a fixed station
Unlock and pay through the Voi app; riders must be 18 or over
Launched across Edinburgh in September 2025

sources.title: City of Edinburgh Council: Cycle hire scheme

title: Lothian Buses and tram fares
summary: Lothian Buses and Edinburgh Trams run the city's public transport network, with single tickets, day tickets and the Ridacard for regular travel.
details: Bus adult single: £2.40; child single: £1.20 (fares from 22 February 2026)
Bus City DAY ticket: £6.00 adult, £3.00 child
Tram adult single £2.40, tram adult DAYticket £6.00
Contactless accepted with automatic daily and weekly capping; on trams you must tap on and tap off
Ridacard season tickets give the lowest fares for regular travel

sources.title: Lothian Buses: Fares revision
Edinburgh Trams: Changes to tram fares in 2026
Lothian Buses: Contactless

title: Find an EV charging point
summary: The council runs a network of on-street and hub EV charge points across Edinburgh, from standard 7kW to rapid 50kW chargers. In 2026 the network moved to WattStop (provided by Fuuse), so older apps and cards may no longer work.
details: Three speeds available: 7kW standard, 22kW fast, 50kW rapid
Pay with the WattStop app, contactless, a QR code, or a roaming card (Octopus Electroverse, ZapMap, Allstar, PAUA)
Find locations via ZapMap; some individual chargers are listed as out of service
22kW charging bays have an 8-hour time limit
Billing queries: electricvehicles.billing@edinburgh.gov.uk

sources.title: City of Edinburgh Council: Find EV charging points
City of Edinburgh Council: Electric vehicles (network changes)

title: Free weekly food waste collection
summary: Nearly every household in Edinburgh gets a weekly food waste collection, at the kerbside for houses or through communal bins for flats, with free caddies to line with any bag you like.
details: Weekly collection for almost all households, kerbside or communal bin
Kitchen caddies and kerbside food bins are ordered free of charge
Line with a compostable liner, plain plastic bag, bread bag, or paper - whatever works
Find your exact collection day by searching your street on the council site

sources.title: City of Edinburgh Council: Food waste prevention and recycling

title: Book a bulky waste (special uplift) collection
summary: Edinburgh Council will collect up to five bulky household items from the kerbside for a small charge, waived for those on Council Tax Reduction.
details: £5 charge per item, up to 5 items per booking
Free if you receive Council Tax Reduction - use the exemption form with your CTR reference
Put items out by 7am on the day of collection
Items must be liftable by two people and no longer than 7 feet
Book online; the booking system has maintenance downtime on Sundays 4am-11am

sources.title: City of Edinburgh Council: Book a bulky waste collection

title: Household waste recycling centres
summary: Edinburgh has three recycling centres for bulky items, garden waste and more - Seafield, Craigmillar and Sighthill - most vehicle visits need a booked slot.
details: Seafield HWRC, 76 Seafield Road, EH6 7LW
Craigmillar HWRC, Old Dalkeith Road, EH16 4TB (pedestrian access currently suspended for safety)
Sighthill HWRC, Bankhead Avenue, EH11 4EA
Open 7 days a week for booked slots; no booking needed on foot or by bike with small amounts
Van and trailer visits need a half-hour slot at 11am, 12:30pm or 2:30pm

sources.title: City of Edinburgh Council: Household waste recycling centres

title: Fix broken items at the Remakery repair cafe
summary: The Edinburgh Remakery runs a weekly pay-what-you-can repair cafe in Leith for clothing, textiles and some electronics, extending the life of things you'd otherwise bin.
details: Every Friday, 11am-1pm, at 13A Newkirkgate Shopping Centre, Leith
Repairs clothing, zips, hems and alterations
Also fixes laptops, desktops, monitors and games consoles (not general electrical goods or software issues)
Pay-what-you-can, drop-in, no booking needed

sources.title: The Edinburgh Remakery: Repair Cafe
